Answer: C
Reason: The serial chest X-rays demonstrate an initial normal radiograph (Figure 1) followed by the development of patchy, peripheral airspace opacities that worsen over time (Figures 2 and 3). This radiographic pattern of migratory or progressive peripheral consolidation is characteristic of Chronic Eosinophilic Pneumonia (CEP), a condition known to show dramatic and complete resolution with corticosteroid therapy.
